title: 1992 AHSME Problem 23
statement: What is the size of the largest subset \(S\) of \(\{1,2,3,\ldots,50\}\) such that no pair of distinct elements of \(S\) has a sum divisible by \(7?\)

solutions.text:
The residue classes \(1,2,\ldots,6,0\) contain \(8,7,7,7,7,7,7\) numbers, respectively. We may take numbers from at most one class in each complementary pair \((1,6),(2,5),(3,4),\) and at most one multiple of \(7.\) Thus \[ \begin{aligned} |S|&\le\max(8,7)+\max(7,7)\\ &\qquad+\max(7,7)+1=23. \end{aligned} \] Taking every number whose residue modulo \(7\) is \(1,\) \(2,\) or \(3,\) together with one multiple of \(7,\) attains \(23.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Group the integers by their residues modulo \(7\)
Pair residue classes \(1\) with \(6,\) \(2\) with \(5,\) and \(3\) with \(4\); treat residue \(0\) separately
